correctness.rationale: For every graph and anchor set A, v_x=1+sqrt(2)d(x,A)>0 and every normalized anchor/edge measurement has squared inner product with v at most one. Thus Rayleigh yields λ_min M≤1/S. A breadth-first rooted forest supplies positive subtree masses H_x and probabilities p_a=H_a/S, p_edge=sqrt(2)H_x/S, normalized because each node contributes v_x(1+sqrt(2)d_x)=v_x² to the sum. Direct balance gives Mv=v/S. Since M has nonpositive off diagonal entries, D(M−S^(-1)I)D is a weighted graph Laplacian when D=diag(v), hence positive semidefinite. Equality in Rayleigh removes all same-distance edges, and eigenvector equations are exactly the nonnegative downhill layer flow balances and anchor formulas; all solutions are valid and normalize automatically. A vertex with two closer neighbors gives two distinct BFS forest choices with positive weights, while unique predecessor fixes every balance; this proves iff uniqueness. Independent numerical eigenchecks on path4, C4, K3, K4 with multiple anchors verified λ_min=1/S and the uniqueness criterion.
